test_title: PYST 55: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 09 Sept, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Babur, the first Mughal ruler, was related to two of the medieval world's greatest conquerors. If he was related to the Mongol conqueror Genghis Khan on his maternal side, to whom was he related on his paternal side?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Timur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Babur was a descendant of Timur (also known as Tamerlane) on his paternal side and was related to Genghis Khan on his maternal side.
 
• Timur was a 14th-century Turco-Mongol conqueror who founded the Timurid Empire in Central Asia.
 
• Babur's lineage connects him to two prominent conquerors: Genghis Khan, known for his vast Mongol Empire, and Timur, renowned for his military campaigns across Asia.
 
• Babur inherited both the legacy of his ancestors and the ambition to establish a powerful empire, which he achieved by founding the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• The connection to Timur on the paternal side was significant as it provided Babur with claims to Central Asia and the prestige of being part of the Timurid dynasty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohammed Ghori:**

 
 
• Mohammed Ghori was a ruler of the Ghurid dynasty who played a pivotal role in establishing Muslim rule in India in the 12th century.
 
• He defeated Prithviraj Chauhan in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 AD), marking the beginning of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Although significant in Indian history, Mohammed Ghori was not related to Babur.
 
 
 
• **Mahmud Ghazni:**
 
 
• Mahmud Ghazni was a ruler of the Ghaznavid dynasty, known for his invasions of India between 1000 and 1027 AD.
 
• He aimed to plunder India's wealth and spread Islam but was not connected to Babur by lineage.
 
• His raids influenced the cultural and political history of medieval India but did not establish any long-lasting dynasty in the region.
 
 
 
• **Ibrahim Lodi:**
 
 
• Ibrahim Lodi was the last Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate's Lodi dynasty.
 
• He was defeated by Babur in the First Battle of Panipat (1526 AD), which marked the beginning of the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• While a significant figure in Babur's conquest of India, Ibrahim Lodi was not related to Babur.
